outreach_drafts.subject: Maria, thank you for being part of Miami’s giving tradition
outreach_drafts.body:
Dear Maria,

Thank you for your Give Miami Day gifts in November 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. We’re grateful for your steady commitment to Miami.

Here’s what we did recently: The Miami Foundation partnered with McDermott Will & Schulte to provide pro bono legal counsel to 17 Miami nonprofits, resulting in 398 hours of service valued at more than $500,000.

That’s a practical way to support local nonprofits: connecting them with professional expertise. We’re proud to share this example of the Foundation’s work as your November giving tradition comes around again.

Will you make a Give Miami Day gift at givemiamiday.org when early giving opens Saturday, November 14, 2026?

Everyone has a role to play. Thank you for the role you’ve played through your giving, Maria, and for considering this year’s celebration.

With gratitude,
The Miami Foundation’s Philanthropy Team
outreach_drafts.call_script:

Update: Here’s what we did recently: The Miami Foundation partnered with McDermott Will & Schulte to provide pro bono legal counsel to 17 Miami nonprofits, resulting in 398 hours of service valued at more than $500,000. We’re proud to share that example of bringing professional expertise to local nonprofits.

Ask: Will you make a Give Miami Day gift at givemiamiday.org when early giving opens Saturday, November 14, 2026?

If Maria says ‘not this year’: Of course, Maria. Thank you for your past generosity and for taking a moment to connect today.

outreach_drafts.subject: Luis, a Miami update ahead of Give Miami Day
outreach_drafts.body:
Luis,

Thank you for giving online each December from 2022 through 2025. We’re grateful for your steady generosity and the local commitment behind it.

Here’s what we’ve been working on: The Jorge M. Pérez Family Foundation at The Miami Foundation announced a $720,000 investment in Miami-Dade County's nonprofit arts sector through its CreARTE grant program.

The Miami Disaster Resilience Fund is also investing $135,000 in resilience hubs and community-based organizations strengthening preparedness across Miami-Dade County. From the arts to preparedness, these are local investments we’re glad to share with you ahead of Give Miami Day.

Please make a Give Miami Day gift at givemiamiday.org when early giving opens Saturday, November 14, 2026.

Everyone has a role to play. Thank you for the generosity you’ve shown over the years.

Warmly,
The Miami Foundation’s Philanthropy Team

research_facts.fact: McDermott hired Jayme Cassidy as Miami-based transactions pro bono counsel in January 2025 to expand legal support for nonprofits, NGOs, small businesses and low-income entrepreneurs in underserved communities.

The Miami office received Legal Services of Greater Miami’s 2023 Equal Justice Pro Bono Large Firm Award for work including transactional clinics and full representation benefiting nonprofits, individuals and low-to-moderate-income small-business owners.
Legal Services of Greater Miami listed McDermott Will & Emery among its Leadership Circle financial donors in its April 2023 newsletter.

outreach_drafts.subject: Thank you for your partnership—let’s connect before Give Miami Day
outreach_drafts.body:
Dear McDermott Will & Schulte team,

Thank you for your partnership and support of The Miami Foundation. We’re grateful to work alongside you in service of Miami.

Here’s what we did together: The Miami Foundation partnered with McDermott Will & Schulte to provide pro bono legal counsel to 17 Miami nonprofits, resulting in 398 hours of service valued at more than $500,000. That partnership is a meaningful example of bringing professional expertise to Miami’s nonprofit community.

With Give Miami Day approaching, would you be open to a call or coffee with our philanthropy team to talk about your year-end giving?

Everyone has a role to play. We’d welcome the chance to hear what matters most to your team and explore how your priorities might connect with Miami’s needs.

With appreciation,
The Miami Foundation’s Philanthropy Team

outreach_drafts.subject: A conversation about Miami and your year-end giving
outreach_drafts.body:
Dear Frederick A. DeLuca Foundation team,

Thank you for your partnership and support of The Miami Foundation. We’re grateful to be connected through a shared commitment to our community.

Here’s a recent update: The Jorge M. Pérez Family Foundation at The Miami Foundation announced a $720,000 investment in Miami-Dade County’s nonprofit arts sector through its CreARTE grant program.

The Miami Foundation also commissioned and unveiled South Dade Community Needs and Nonprofit Funding Landscape, which analyzed more than 1,400 grants to 262 South Dade nonprofits and included interviews with 19 community leaders, providers and advocates.

With Give Miami Day approaching, would you join our philanthropy team for a call or coffee about your year-end giving? We’d welcome the chance to hear what matters most to your team and share more about this work here in Miami.

Everyone has a role to play. Thank you for your partnership.

Warmly,
The Miami Foundation’s Philanthropy Team

outreach_drafts.subject: Give Miami Day: a conversation about your year-end giving
outreach_drafts.body:
Dear Biscayne Harbor Family Foundation team,

Thank you for your partnership and support of The Miami Foundation. We’re grateful to have you alongside us in Miami.

Here’s what we’ve done recently: we commissioned and unveiled South Dade Community Needs and Nonprofit Funding Landscape. The report analyzed more than 1,400 grants to 262 South Dade nonprofits and included interviews with 19 community leaders, providers and advocates.

Inspired directly by that report, Amazon announced a $1 million investment in 13 South Dade nonprofit organizations to strengthen their capacity and deepen their community impact. It’s a local example of research helping inform investment in our community.

With Give Miami Day approaching, would you join our philanthropy team for a call or coffee about your year-end giving? We’d welcome the chance to hear what matters most to you.

Everyone has a role to play. Thank you for yours.

Warmly,
The Miami Foundation’s Philanthropy Team

It analyzed more than 1,400 grants to 262 South Dade nonprofits and included interviews with 19 community leaders, providers and advocates. Inspired directly by the report, Amazon announced a $1 million investment in 13 South Dade nonprofit organizations to strengthen their capacity and deepen their community impact.

Ask: With Give Miami Day approaching, would you join our philanthropy team for a call or coffee about your year-end giving? We’d love to hear what matters most to you.

If not this year: Of course—thank you for letting us know, and for your partnership and support.

9.full_name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
9.org_name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation

research_facts.fact: Knight awarded $3 million in November 2022 to establish the Miami-Dade Innovation Authority, supporting technology adoption in climate resilience, health and financial inclusion.
The Miami Foundation administers the Knight-supported Esserman-Knight Journalism Awards, recognizing investigative and public-service reporting in Miami-Dade, Broward and Monroe counties.
In January 2021, Amazon announced $500,000 for United Way organizations in Miami-Dade and Broward counties to support vulnerable families during the pandemic.
